I'm a 44-year-old woman who's been farming these 10.1 mu in Quzhou for 20 years. My family has six people, but my husband and eldest son work construction in the county town, so most days it's me, my mother-in-law, and my daughter handling the land. That means labor is tight—I can't take on more than we can manage.

I split the farm into two parts. About 6 mu I keep in wheat-maize double cropping—that's our grain and basic food security. The other 4.1 mu I plant cotton. Cotton earns more cash per mu, but it's backbreaking work, especially picking. With my husband and son away, I have to hire help for cotton picking, which costs money I don't always have.

For the **winter wheat** on those 6 mu, I planted last October like always. I'm not changing the variety—it's the same improved wheat my neighbor grows, and I bought fresh seed this year because my saved seed was losing vigor. I put down about 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu at planting time. Come spring, when the wheat starts jointing, I'll topdress with another 50 jin of urea per mu. The extension agent keeps telling us to reduce fertilizer, but two years ago I cut back and my yield dropped by nearly 50 kg per mu—I lost money. So I'm sticking with what works. I'll irrigate three times: once when the wheat greens up in March, once at jointing, and once at heading. Pumping water isn't cheap—each time costs me about 20 yuan per mu—but three times is the minimum if I want a decent crop. I'll spray herbicide once in spring. I expect about 420 kg per mu if the weather cooperates.

**Summer maize** goes in right after wheat harvest in mid-June. There's no time to waste—the custom combine harvests the wheat, and within a day or two I need that maize in the ground or I miss the season. I hire a tractor with a planter because we can't do it by hand fast enough. I put all the fertilizer down at planting: about 100 jin per mu total, split as 50 jin compound fertilizer and 30 jin urea. There's no time to come back and side-dress later, and summer usually brings some rain. I'll irrigate once in July if it turns dry, otherwise I rely on rainfall. I spray herbicide right after planting. If things go normally, I should get around 480 kg per mu.

For **cotton** on the 4.1 mu, I plant in late April. I plow in early spring and harrow before planting. I use about 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, then topdress with 30 jin of urea when flowering starts. Cotton needs water at flowering and boll-setting, so I'll irrigate twice. The biggest headache is pests—bollworm especially. I'll spray insecticide three or four times and herbicide once. Picking is what kills me. I'll pick what I can with family, but I'll need to hire about 10 days of labor for the peak picking period. Hired hands cost about 120 yuan per day now, but I have no choice. I expect about 280 kg of seed cotton per mu.

I wanted to put more fertilizer on the wheat, but my daughter needs school fees in the fall, and we always keep some cash for emergencies. I'd rather apply a bit too much fertilizer than too little—losing a whole crop hurts far more than wasting a few dozen yuan on extra urea. Total costs this year will run me about 7,600 yuan, which is most of what I have set aside. If prices hold, that should cover costs and leave enough for the family. That's the plan.
